A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original downstream evaluations on three MoE models, load-balancing measurements, expert-behavior analyses, and loss ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds sensitivity, inference-budget, mixed-training, baseline, architecture, and timing results in Tables 3–9.

M1.justification: The auxiliary, orthogonality, and variance objectives in Equations 5–7 and the existing LoRA procedure are retained. Appendix H.1 newly documents dynamic loss normalization but does not identify it as a procedural revision; this is additional implementation disclosure.

E1.justification: The eleven evaluation benchmarks and their underlying domains remain unchanged. Appendix H.3 adds joint post-training on combined Numina, GPQA, and HumanEval data, testing heterogeneous math/science/code adaptation alongside the original task-specific settings.

E2.justification: The four original comparators remain in Table 1. Table 7 adds ERNIE 4.5 LBL and SIMBAL, substantially extending the balancing-method comparisons. Table 4 also adds pretrained base-model controls, distinct from the existing fine-tuning ablation without auxiliary losses.

E3.justification: New protocols include coefficient reductions from 10^-3 to 10^-4, generation budgets of 512/1024/2048 tokens, mixed-data training on 18,000 examples for three epochs, and evaluation on Mixtral and Phi-MoE. Table 9 introduces iteration-time measurement on DeepSeek V2 Lite at batch size 32. Existing LoRA defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained loss-removal ablations, v3 adds coefficient sensitivity analysis, generation-length sensitivity, and an experiment jointly increasing training-data size and diversity in Appendix H. These substantially broaden robustness analysis. The earlier PCA evidence is retained through redisplay.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains its uncertainty entries and the existing statement about multiple measurements. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added. The new appendix tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original plotted results are unchanged, but Tables 3–9 add substantial results under additional conditions. For example, Table 7 reports GSM8K scores of 50.94 for Ours, 48.75 for SIMBAL, and 47.24 for ERNIE 4.5 LBL. Table 9 reports 11.5 seconds/iteration for Ours versus 10.7 for Only Aux.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical definitions, gradient derivations, lemmas, and proofs are retained. New Appendix C.4 adds a computational-complexity argument giving O(N k^2 d) cost for pairwise expert-output projections. Equations 44–45 merely restate the existing objective.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain complementary orthogonality and variance objectives that improve specialization and downstream performance while preserving load balance without architectural changes. The headline 23.79% improvement claim and conclusion are unchanged; the introduction clarifies an already established post-training focus.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning hyperparameter robustness, applicability beyond task-specific training, architectural generality, and computational tradeoffs. Appendix H.2 newly attributes score discrepancies to checkpoint, prompting, and generation-budget differences and acknowledges resource limits. Some interpretation is overstated: Appendix I.2 claims wins across all tasks despite the Mixtral HumanEval exception in Table 8.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a code hyperlink instead of promising release and newly documents 6,000 examples per benchmark, teacher-generated and manually verified answers, three training epochs, router/expert LoRA placement, dynamic loss scaling, and zero-shot 512-token evaluation. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond the retained Appendix F settings, without establishing changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to the ERNIE 4.5 technical report and Load Balancing Mixture of Experts with Similarity Preserving Routers, with corresponding positioning in Appendix I.1. The main related-work discussion and other cited works are retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization remain intact. Changes include a clarified introduction, expanded setup paragraphs, new cross-references, acknowledgements, and additional appendix sections. The visualization appendix moves from H to K; there is no extensive rewriting of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds seven result tables, expands Figure 1's caption, and relocates Figure 2. The twelve unchanged PCA plots from v2's Figures 5–6 are consolidated into one much smaller 4-by-3 Figure 5, substantially changing their presentation and reducing label readability.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 improves experimental transparency and supplies useful sensitivity, broader-comparison, and training-cost evidence. These gains are limited by missing uncertainty for the added experiments and overstated interpretations: Table 8 reports Mixtral HumanEval at 37.73 for Ours versus 39.74 for AuxOnly despite the claim of wins across all tasks. The compressed PCA figure also loses readability. The additions support a positive but limited overall quality improvement.
